exec: A local Russian centre's website went offline; the centre says a targeted cyberattack may be the cause. Unconfirmed, for awareness.
plain: The website of the Stalin Center in Barnaul, Russia stopped working on 21 November. The centre says early information suggests a targeted cyberattack could be the cause. Its venue is open as normal.

key_findings: The centre's website stopped working on the afternoon of 21 November and is temporarily unavailable.
According to the centre, preliminary data suggest the cause could have been a targeted cyberattack.
The centre says it is restoring the site, preserving materials and strengthening information security; the physical venue continues to operate normally.

summary: MK Barnaul reports that the website of the Stalin Center in Barnaul stopped working on the afternoon of 21 November and is temporarily unavailable. The centre told the paper that, according to preliminary data, the outage could have been caused by a targeted cyberattack; the report does not say an attack was confirmed. The centre says it is restoring the site and strengthening information security, and its venue continues to operate normally.
title: Barnaul Stalin Center website down; centre says a targeted cyberattack may be the cause

validation.note: Only MK Barnaul read; it relays the centre's own preliminary statement. No other publisher or statement on the centre's channels found.

review.note: wording: 'no attack has been confirmed' was CyberView's conclusion; now 'the report does not say an attack was confirmed'. Date, outage category, centre's statement checked against MK Barnaul
